oneLine: Keeps the warehouse's catalogue of process paths and each site's carrier cut-off schedule, and tells the rest of the fleet whenever either changes.

rows.title: Define a new process path
rows.story: An operator adds a path to the catalogue: its name prefix, the skills it needs, its p95 cycle time and which demand sources may feed it. A path id is never reused, even after retirement.

then.does: adds the path to its catalogue copy, so released work for it is accepted and gets its required skills
adds the path to its catalogue copy, so work can be planned onto it
adds the path to its catalogue copy, so shift plans and assignments can name it
adds the path, with its cycle time and eligibility, to the copy it uses to route orders
adds the path's cycle time to the copy it uses for capacity figures

rows.title: Revise a process path
rows.story: An operator changes an active path's prefix, skills, cycle time, eligibility or intake. If nothing actually changed, nothing is announced. The full new definition is sent, never a diff.

then.does: replaces its copy of the path definition
replaces its copy of the path definition
replaces its copy of the path definition
replaces its copy, so the next delivery promise uses the new cycle time and eligibility
replaces the cycle time it uses for capacity figures

rows.title: Retire a process path
rows.story: An operator retires a path for good. It is refused while any site's cut-off schedule still lists the path, so the operator revises those schedules first.
reads: Sites whose schedule lists the path

then.does: removes the path from its catalogue copy
removes the path from its catalogue copy
removes the path from its catalogue copy
removes the path from its copy, so no order is routed onto it
removes the path from its capacity copy

rows.title: Publish a site's cut-off schedule
rows.story: An operator sets, or replaces in full, a site's carrier cut-off times. Every path a cut-off lists must be active. An identical schedule changes nothing and announces nothing.

then.does: replaces the site's cut-off windows it uses to promise delivery times
replaces the site's cut-offs it uses for capacity figures
replaces its copy of the site's cut-off schedule
stores the site's cut-offs as a view; it books no appointment from them yet

rows.title: Replay every active path at start-up
rows.story: When the service starts, it announces the current definition of each active path again. This way a consumer that rebuilds its catalogue from scratch never misses a path whose first event has aged out.
rows.policy: Whenever the service starts, announce every active path again

then.does: a fresh instance rebuilds its catalogue copy from the replay
a fresh instance rebuilds its catalogue copy from the replay
a fresh instance rebuilds its catalogue copy from the replay

rows.title: Replay every site's schedule at start-up
rows.story: In the same start-up pass, the current cut-off schedule of each site is announced again, in full, for the same reason: a fresh consumer must be able to rebuild its copy.
rows.policy: Whenever the service starts, announce every site's schedule again

then.does: a fresh instance rebuilds its cut-off copy from the replay
a fresh instance rebuilds its cut-off copy from the replay

rows.title: Count catalogue growth for reports
rows.story: The service reads its own path announcements and keeps a daily tally of paths defined, revised and retired, which feeds the catalogue growth report. It never reads another context's events.
rows.policy: Whenever a path is created, revised or retired, add one to that day's tally

hotspots.text: The site id of a cut-off schedule is never checked. A schedule for an unknown site only shows up later as an unroutable order in order-management.
ICQA (inventory control) is deliberately left undecided: it may become a path family, stay in inventory-storage, or call into it.
wes-work-planning and network-inventory-planning do not yet filter on the declared intake values; they route by explicit path id.
How long announcements are kept is not set here. Consumers rebuild their copy by replaying them all, so the start-up replay is the safety net.

opportunities.text: Log compaction would let the broker keep only the latest announcement per path and per site. It is a warehouse-infra change.
If the fleet gets a real transportation context, the cut-off schedule can move there unchanged. Its place here is provisional.
